title: The Punic Wars (264–146 BCE)
key_facts: Three wars fought between the Roman Republic and Carthage for dominance in the western Mediterranean
First Punic War centered on naval control of Sicily; Second featured Hannibal’s campaigns; Third ended with the destruction of Carthage
Paved the way for Roman hegemony across the Mediterranean
causes: Competition over trade routes, allies, and territory in Sicily and the western Mediterranean
Escalating rivalries between expanding Rome and maritime Carthage
Allied disputes and interventions that triggered wider war
outcome: Rome’s victory and annexation of key Carthaginian territories
Carthage’s power broken and city destroyed in 146 BCE
Acceleration of Roman expansion and militarization

figures.name: Hannibal Barca
figures.role: Carthaginian general of the Second Punic War

figures.name: Scipio Africanus
figures.role: Roman general who defeated Hannibal at Zama

impacts: Established Rome as the preeminent Mediterranean power
Set administrative and economic patterns for Roman provinces
Long-term transformation of Roman society and politics
